en: The northeast monsoon (amihan) brings cool, dry air to the Philippines because winds blow from high-pressure areas in Asia toward the equator.
Plants release water vapor into the air through tiny leaf pores called stomata, which adds moisture to the atmosphere during the water cycle.
Limestone transforms into marble when intense underground heat and pressure squeeze and recrystallize its calcite minerals without melting the rock.
Earth experiences different seasons because its tilted axis points the Northern or Southern hemisphere toward the Sun as it orbits the star.
The Moon's gravity pulls Earth's ocean water toward it, creating a bulge that causes high tides on the side facing the Moon.
Underwater earthquakes displace massive amounts of ocean water, generating powerful tsunami waves that travel rapidly across the sea toward coastlines.
Fast-flowing river water picks up and carries away loose topsoil from riverbanks, gradually eroding the land and changing the river's shape.
Stars shine because extreme core pressure and temperature force hydrogen atoms to fuse into helium, releasing massive amounts of light and heat energy.
Land heats up faster than the ocean during the day, causing warm air over land to rise and cool ocean air to rush inland.
When hot magma erupts from a volcano and contacts cold surface air, it rapidly cools and solidifies into extrusive igneous rock.
Heavy rainfall saturates soil on steep slopes, adding weight and reducing friction, which causes the dirt and rocks to slide downhill.
Warm, moist air rises and cools in the upper atmosphere, causing invisible water vapor to condense into visible liquid cloud droplets.
